findings.title: Reminders with no message or recipient are never counted or deleted
findings.body: The retry increment only runs when twilio.scheduleSMS returns null or throws. If message is empty/null or sendTo is falsy, the `if (message?.length && ... && sendTo)` block is skipped entirely: the reminder stays unscheduled with retryCount 0, is re-fetched on every cron run, and the new `retryCount > 1` cleanup never fires. This leaves the exact infinite-rescheduling loop the PR aims to fix in place for missing/invalid phone numbers or empty templates (and similarly for the `continue` at lines 68-70 when workflowStep/booking is missing, which also never increments).

findings.title: Retry increment is a stale read-modify-write, not atomic
findings.body: Both increments (lines 184 and 195) write `reminder.retryCount + 1` using the value snapshotted by the findMany at the start of the run. If two cron invocations overlap, both read retryCount 0 and both write 1, so the counter never exceeds 1, the `retryCount > 1` deletion never triggers, and failing reminders are retried forever (and may also double-schedule with Twilio). Using Prisma's atomic `{ increment: 1 }` avoids the lost update.

findings.title: Unhandled update inside catch can abort the whole cron run
findings.body: The catch block now awaits `prisma.workflowReminder.update` without its own error handling. If that update fails (e.g. P2025 because the reminder was deleted by the concurrent cleanup/another run, or a transient DB error), the exception propagates out of the per-reminder try/catch, aborting the loop so all remaining unscheduled reminders are skipped and the handler returns 500 instead of `SMS scheduled`. Previously the catch only logged. The increment should be wrapped so a failure to record a retry does not break processing of the other reminders.

findings.title: Retry-count deletion clause is not scoped to SMS reminders
findings.body: The original deleteMany was scoped to `method: SMS`; in the new OR the second branch `{ retryCount: { gt: 1 } }` has no method (or scheduled/date) constraint, so it deletes WorkflowReminder rows of any method (EMAIL/WHATSAPP share this table per WorkflowMethods) once their retryCount exceeds 1, even if they are future-dated and not this SMS cron's responsibility. Scoping it to SMS (like the first branch) keeps this handler from deleting other channels' reminders.
